title: Masters Edition III: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: "Healing is a matter of time, but it is sometimes also a matter of opportunity." —D'Avenant proverb
Quick and agile, Amrou Kithkin can usually escape from even the most fearsome opponents.
The clouds broke and the sun's rays burst forth; each foul beast in its turn faltered, and was gone.
Avenant's archers are also trained as poets, so that each arrow is guided by a fragment of verse.
Though they often bore little greater charm than the demons they battled, exorcists were always welcome in Scarwood.
"All warfare is based on deception." —Sun Tzu, Art of War (trans. Giles)
"He Guan Yu covered the ground on a thousand-li horse;/ With dragon blade he took each pass by force."
"Sometimes even the smallest boon can save a life." —Halvor Arenson, Kjeldoran Priest
The elite guard of the Mesa High Priests, the Ivory Guardians, were created to protect the innocent and faithful. Some say their actions are above the law.
"Such a lord as this—all virtues' height—Had never been, nor ever was again."
"If you do it right, they'll never know what hit them." —General Jarkeld, the Arctic Fox
"Only wisdom and virtue can truly win men's devotion." —Liu Bei
The mourning families of commanders and generals were often given land, valuables, or money to compensate for their losses.
"We three, though of separate ancestry, join in brotherhood. . . . We dare not hope to be together always but hereby vow to die the selfsame day." —Peach Garden Oath
In establishing the Shu kingdom, Liu Bei's forces fought against Ma Chao at Chengdu. Eventually, Ma Chao surrendered and became one of Liu Bei's Tiger Generals.
Throughout the three kingdoms, important generals were often guarded by small groups of expert soldiers known as "elite companions."
During Kongming's campaigns against the Wei, his Shu troops rotated from the battlefront to the fields every hundred days.
As many attackers were dazzled by the wall's beauty as were halted by its force.
Zhang Fei's uncharacteristic alliance with a defeated Riverlands general, Yan Yan, allowed Shu forces to advance through forty-five Riverlands strongpoints with no casualties.
The rising oceans brought new lakes—and new terrors—to Terisiare. The Explorers found their ancient enemies spawning everywhere.
"O! call back yesterday, bid time return." —William Shakespeare, King Richard the Second
Kongming and Lu Su tricked Wei troops into shooting over 100,000 arrows at them to later use against the Wei at Red Cliffs.
At Red Cliffs, Kongming and Zhou Yu each wrote his plan for defeating Wei on the palm of his hand. They laughed as they both revealed the same word, "Fire."
The province of Jingzhou was the fulcrum of the three kingdoms. At separate times it was coveted and controlled by the Wu, the Shu, and the Wei.
Many people say that no power can bring the mountains low. Many people are fools.
"Leadership, not numbers, determines victory." —A Wu commander, before his 5,000 troops forced 15,000 Wei troops to retreat from Ruxu
"The potential for change lies in all things. Know a thing's nature, know its possibilities, and know it anew." —Gustha Ebbasdotter, Kjeldoran Royal Mage
"I doubt any labyrinth minotaurs still live—but then again, we minotaurs are stubborn beings." —Onatah, Anaba Shaman
As the Wu chief commander, Lu Meng conquered Shu-held Jingzhou in 219 by disguising soldiers as merchants on boats filled with hiding troops.
Nethya stiffened suddenly, head cocked as if straining to hear some distant sound, then felt lifeless to the ground.
"It's nice to see a sister Dwarf in a position of such power, but why'd it have to be one of those seafaring muleheads?" —Halina, Dwarven Trader
"Plans evolved within the tent decide a victory 1,000 li away."
"One score and four he reigned, the Southland king: / A dragon coiled, a tiger poised below the mighty Yangtze."
At the second battle of Ruxu, the brave Wu general Gan Ning raided Cao Cao's camp of 400,000 men with only 100 cavalry. Not a single man or horse was lost.
Both Wu and Wei warships patrolled the Yangtze River, the natural border between the two kingdoms.
"All rivers eventually run to the sea. My job is to sort out who goes first." —Maeveen O'Donagh, Memoirs of a Soldier
Some say Banshees are the hounds of Death, baying to herd their prey into the arms of their master.
"'War is no picnic,' my father liked to say. But the ants seemed to disagree." —General Chanek Valteroth
"Then flashed the living lightning from her eyes,/ And screams of horror rend th' affrighted skies." —Alexander Pope, The Rape of the Lock
"Lieutenants dishonored, corpses carted home; The general raises troops again to take revenge."
"But it was a year of dearth. People were reduced to eating leaves of jujube trees. Corpses were seen everywhere in the countryside."
"The burst of strength brought on by this plague should not be mistaken for a sign of renewed health." —Kolbjörn, High Honored Druid
Cao Cao was haunted to death by the ghosts of the empresses and other high courtiers he had murdered.
The voices of the dead ring in the heart long after they have faded from the ears.
One who goes unpunished never learns. —Greek proverb
"High on a throne of royal state . . . insatiate to pursue vain war with heav'n." —John Milton, Paradise Lost
These days, some wizards are finding that they have a little too much spell left at the end of their mana.
At the battle of Guandu, Cao Cao defeated Yuan Shao by raiding his grain depot, leaving him with no way to feed his troops.
"An immense river of oblivion is sweeping us away into a nameless abyss." —Ernest Renan, Souvenirs d'Enfance et de Jeunesse
Cao Cao was more concerned with capabilities than lineage. He excelled at recruiting and retaining men of talent to serve him.
Wei won the battle of Hefei when Zhang Liao defeated Sun Quan and then foiled a Wu scheme to incite rebellion.
At the battle of Chang'an, Ma Chao defeated the two generals Cao Cao sent to guard the pass but was forced to flee when Cao Cao's trickery turned his own ally against him.
"To send the common people to war untrained is to throw them away." —Confucius, The Analects (trans. Lau)
"The Ancestors are the wisdom of the tribe and the soul of the Homelands. I am eternally in their debt." —Taysir
"The Spirit Crafters sing of all our people. They sing of those lost, of those found, and of those who are yet to be." —Onatah, Anaba Shaman
When the sky's rain has turned to fire, what will put it out?
"Kobolds are harmless." —Bearand the Bold, epitaph
Noted neither for their good looks nor their charm, manticores can be fearsome allies. As dinner companions, however, they are best left alone.
"With fire he broke the battle at Bowang . . . . Striking fear deep into Cao Cao's soul, thus Kongming scored a coup at his debut."
Brimstone marks this drake's territory. Unfortunately for travelers, all of the Burning Isles smell likewise.
"The bird of wonder dies, the maiden phoenix,/ Her ashes new-create another heir/ As great in admiration as herself." —William Shakespeare, King Henry the Eighth
The frost giants have been out in the cold a long, long time, but they have their rage to keep them warm.

The minotaurs of the Hurloon Mountains are known for their love of battle. They are also known for their hymns to the dead, sung for friend and foe alike. These hymns can last for days, filling the mountain valleys with their low, haunting sounds.
"Joining this army is easy, boy. Just survive your first battle."
"One for all, all for one; we strike first, and then you're done!" —Oath of the Kobold Musketeers
The Taskmaster knows that there is no cure for the common Kobold.
Kher Keep is unique among fortresses: impervious to aerial assault but defenseless from the ground.
"Dong Zhuo's man, Lu Bu, warrior without peer,/ Far surpassed the champions of his sphere."
The only thing worse than a minotaur with an axe is an angry minotaur with an axe.
". . . The kingdoms three are now the stuff of dream,/ For men to ponder, past all praise or blame."
They are aberrations who have turned on everything we hold sacred. Let them be cast out." —Ailheen, Speaker of the Council
"Faeries talk all in riddles and tricky bits, 'cept the Nobles. Now, there's some straight talkers." —Joskun, An-Havva Constable
The lion's only loyalty is to its hunger.
The communal mind produces a savage strategy, yet no one could predict that this vicious crossbreed would unravel the secret of steel.
The stubborn Meng Huo was captured and released by Kongming seven times before finally surrendering.
Through his allies, Meng Huo commanded several hundred thousand troops composed of cavalry, rattan-armored warriors, infantry, naked men with swords, and wild animals.
"All men have their appointed time; that's something no horse can change." —Liu Bei, after being told that the Dilu brings its master ill fortune
The only sound was the gentle clicking of the faeries' wings. Then those intruders who were still standing turned and fled. One thing was certain: they didn't think the scryb were very funny anymore.
"Unless you enter the tiger's lair, you cannot get hold of the tiger's cubs." —Sun Tzu, Art of War (trans. Giles)
"Trying to meet a worthy man in the wrong way is as bad as closing the door on an invited guest." —Mencius, a Chinese philosopher
Trip wire, hooked poles, and sunken pits were commonly used to unhorse riders during the Three Kingdoms period.
"Those of faith are those of strength." —Autumn Willow
"Battles no longer served a purpose in Karakas." —Angus Mackenzie, Diary
He is devious and cunning, in both appearance and deed. Beware the Warbeard, for this brute bites as well as he barks!
Thundering down from Hammerheim, no foe could slow Bartel's charge.
Urborg became the final resting place of many swordsmen of renown, their steel outmatched by the wiles of Gwendlyn.
Hail from Tolaria the ever changing 'Dane.
"You would never guess, at the terrifying sight of the man, that Hunding was as charming a companion as one could wish for."
Mightiest of the cat warriors, Jedit Ojanen forsook the forests of his tribe and took service with the Robaran Mercenaries, rising through their ranks to lead them in the battle for Efrava.
Once, the order of the Closed Fist reached throughout the Kb'Briann Highlands. Now, Jerrard alone remains to uphold their standard.
"Two of my Warriors found that the creature was dangerous not only in combat, but also in simple proximity." —Disa the Restless, journal entry
"When milady was young, the sight of a rainbow would fill her soul with peace. As she grew, she learned to share her rapture with others." —Lady Gabriella

"I do not remember what he said to her. I remember her fiery eyes, fixed upon him for an instant. I remember a flash, and the hot breath of sudden flames made me turn away. When I looked again, Angus was gone." —A Wayfarer, on meeting Lady Orca
Livonya's own nature is a matter of mystery. Nothing is known for sure, merely rumors of unearthly stealth, and unholy alliances.
Marhault Elsdragon follows a strict philosophy, never letting emotions cloud his thoughts. No chance observer could imagine the rage in his heart.
We all know the legend: Pavel wanders the realms, helping those in greatest need. But is this a measure of his generosity, or of his obligation to atone?
"On the field of honor, a soldier need have no fear."
Ramirez DePietro is a most flamboyant pirate. Be careful not to believe his tall tales, especially when you ask his age.
"Political violence is a perfectly legitimate answer to the persecution handed down by dignitaries of the state."
"Remember Sir Shandlar! Remember and stand firm!" —rallying cry of the Eberyn militia
Even the brave have cause to tremble at the sight of Sivitri Scarzam. Who else has tamed Scarzam's Dragon?
"What can be a stronger shield than concealment? Have you ever defeated an enemy you didn't know existed?" —Gerda Äagesdotter, Archmage of the Unseen
Sunastian has roots in both sorcery and swordplay; he has learned never to depend too heavily on the latter.
Her given name has been lost in the mists of time. Legend says that her silent vigil will one day be ended by the one who, pure of heart and spirit, calls out that name again.
Administrator of the military state of Sheoltun, Tobias is the military right arm of the empire and the figurehead of its freedom.
"How can you accuse me of evil? Though these deeds be unsavory, no one will argue: good shall follow from them."
An explorer of the Æther, Tuknir often discovers himself in the most unusual physical realms.
A regular guest at the Royal Masquerade, Arien is the envy of the Court. She appears in a new costume every hour.
For a dozen years the Cage had held Lord Ith, but as the Pretender Mairsil's power weakened, so did the bars.
After the Battle of Pitdown, Lady Ursnell fashioned the first such instrument out of Lord Ursnell's left leg.
"Three such creatures stood burning at the crest of the hill. Only seconds later, the fireball struck our front line." —Lydia, Countess Brellis
"Play the song of he who delivered us. Play the song of Feroz." —Onatah, Anaba Shaman
"What do you have that I cannot obtain?" —Mairsil, called the Pretender
"Look deep into the Grail, and see there what you desire most." —Gerda Äagesdotter, Archmage of the Unseen
"'Tis distance lends enchantment to the view,/ And robes the mountain in its azure hue." —Thomas Campbell, "Pleasures of Hope"
"To make a prairie it takes a clover and one bee,/ One clover, and a bee,/ And revery." —Emily Dickinson

"Resignedly beneath the sky/The melancholy waters lie./So blend the turrets and shadows there/That all seem pendulous in air,/While from a proud tower in town/Death looks gigantically down." —Edgar Allan Poe, "The City in the Sea"
